newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southern Baptists boycott "gay friendly" Disney.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southern Baptists boycott "gay friendly" Disney.

text.p: Southern Baptists launched a boycott against Walt Disney Co. and its subsidiaries on Wednesday, accusing the entertainment giant of abandoning its wholesome image of the past to promote homosexuality.

The sweeping boycott of Disney's theme parks, stores and all of its subsidiaries -- including ABC television and radio -- was overhwelmingly approved by delegates of the Southern Baptist Convention, the nation's largest Protestant denomination, at an annual meeting in Dallas.

Rev. Richard Land, president of the Southern Baptists' Christian Life Commission, predicted many of the denomination's 15.7 million members nationwide would follow the call to cut out family trips to Disney World and Disney superstores, as well as boycott its subsidiaries.
"Disney is going to find out just how many regiments and just how many divisions of godly people Southern Baptists have," Land said in proposing the boycott.

Disney has drawn the anger of Southern Baptists and other conservative religious groups because it offers health benefits to the partners of its homosexual employees and allowed "Gay Days" organised by gay rights groups at its theme parks.

Southern Baptists warned last June they would give Disney one year to respond to their objections but Land said the multibillion dollar company simply increased what he described as its "anti-family, pro-gay" policies and programming.
"On good days, the Disney corporation ignored us. On bad days, they contemptuously gave us the back of their hands," Land told thousands of delegates, or messengers.

Conservative critics have for several years complained about the sex and violence in movies made by Disney and its subsidiaries. Some like "Pulp Fiction" and "Kids" were aimed at adult audiences, but even some of Disney's trademark animated movies for children have come under attack.

The American Family Association claimed "The Lion King" includes a homosexual relationship between a meerkat and a wart hog, and "The Little Mermaid" has a scene depicting a priest being sexually aroused while presiding over a wedding.

The final straw for Disney's critics came earlier this year when actress Ellen DeGeneres and the character she plays in "Ellen", a popular sitcom on Disney-owned ABC television, announced they were lesbians.
Southern Baptist leaders said the "Ellen" episode showed Disney had no intention of meeting their requests for more traditional family entertainment.
"The only response we have seen is the further promotion of the homosexual lifestyle," said Land, who led the Southern Baptists' year-long review of Disney policies and products.

The resolution passed on Wednesday calls on all Southern Baptists "to take the stewardship of their time, money and resources so seriously that they refrain from patronising The Disney Company and any of its related entities".
Disney officials declined to comment on the impact of any boycott but said the company had nothing to be ashamed of.
"We are very proud that Disney creates more family entertainment of every kind than anyone else in the world, and we plan to increase that production," spokesman Ken Green said.
Gay rights activists say Disney is one of a growing number of companies that have dropped discriminatory policies, and that the Southern Baptists are out of tune with mainstream American society.

"They are overestimating the anti-gay sentiment in their own organisation and the country," said David Smith, a spokesman for the Human Rights Campaign gay rights group which lobbies Congress and big U.S. companies.
